To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the brain contains many body representations, (2) the cortical representations of one's own arm and hand are systematically different in the two hemispheres for right-handed individuals, and (3) the cortical representations are symmetrical across the two hemispheric halves for left-handed individuals.

right-handed people perceive their right hands and arms as being longer than their left hands and arms, and this asymmetry is related to differences in cortical representation of the hands and arms between hemispheres.
right-handed people tend to over-estimate the length of their right arm and right-hand and left-handed people tend to perceive their arm length accurately.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain represents and perceives the body.
the neural representation of body parts, and how this representation relates to conscious perception of the size and location of the body.
how the brain perceives and represents the body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain contains many body representations, and these representations differ in size between right- and left-handed people.

there is a strong link between the body maps in the cortex and the way we perceive the body, and that the body maps in our brain are not static and fixed, but are dynamic and plastic, and can change in size depending on the task at hand.
there is an association between the size of the cortical representation of the right hand/arm in the left hemisphere and the perceived length of the right arm/hand in right-handed people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain's implicit representation of the body influences the perception of the body.
the body representation in the brain is asymmetric in right-handed individuals, whereas it is symmetric in left-handed individuals.
the body maps are not static, but rather dynamic and flexible, changing with the context and the task at hand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found a relationship between implicit neural body representations and conscious perception.
there are important links between the way we represent our own body in our brains and the way that we perceive our own body.
the brain is a powerful source of perceptual biases, and that the body is no exception.
